issues.location: scripts/lib/repo_invariants.py:535-543 (workflow_problems: the '#' skip runs before the run-script check)
issues.problem: Comment-looking lines inside a run: block scalar are skipped before the ${{ }} check. But the '#' line is script text, and GitHub interpolates ${{ }} before the shell runs. So '# echo "${{ github.event.comment.body }}"' (a commented-out line, the classic accidental form) is a live injection, because a body containing a newline escapes the shell comment. The check passes it silently, for both | and > scalars.
issues.evidence:
REVF-H3b-r2-probe/wf_probe.py on HARDENED with '      - run: |
          echo hi
          # ${{ github.event.comment.body }}': MISSED []; same with '>' and '#${{ github.event.issue.body }}': MISSED. PyYAML: {'run': 'echo hi
# ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
'} (REVF-H3b-r2-probe/wf_yaml.py). The real workflows have no such line today (grep), so the change can land without churn.
issues.suggested_fix: Move the 'number <= script_until' check above the comment skip, or skip '#' lines only outside script and scalar extents. Add a test for a commented ${{ github.event.* }} line inside both | and > run scripts.

issues.problem: R13-11 is still not complete. graph.json keeps the maintainer's username in the flattened form 'users_<name>_projects_silver_bullet...' (4 occurrences, 2 node ids: the session-*-users_<name>_projects_silver_bullet_repo node and the sb_product_overview..._users_<name>_projects_silver_bulle node). The previous review listed this form explicitly. The invariant cannot catch it, because FLAT_HOME's lookahead ends in \b and there is no word boundary between 'projects' and '_silver'. Other forms the guard also misses: /mnt/c/Users/<n> (WSL; the lookbehind fails after 'c'), lowercase users-<n>-projects (FLAT_HOME is not re.I), _home_<n>_ (the lean-ctx Linux form), \\/Users\\/<n> (double-escaped JSON), \u002fUsers\u002f<n>, ~<n>/, and Users.<n>.
issues.evidence: git show 2f7a418:graphify-out/graph.json | grep -oiE 'users_<name>_' | wc -l -> 4 (value not printed; name read from names.txt). The personal-data check on the worktree returns rc=0 in 10.7 s. REVF-H3b-r2-probe/pd_probe.py: graph_id MISSED, mnt_users MISSED, Users_lower_dash MISSED, home_under MISSED, double_json_esc MISSED, unicode_esc MISSED, tilde MISSED; users_dash, lean, home_dash, var_home, json_esc, url, lower, upper, file_uri CAUGHT.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace \b with (?![A-Za-z0-9]) or [-_./] in the FLAT_HOME lookahead and compile FLAT_HOME with re.I. Allow any non-alnum (or a drive letter) before /Users in HOME_PATH (for /mnt/c/Users), and add _home_. Decode \u002f and repeated backslash-escapes before matching. Scrub the 2 node ids in graph.json (regenerate or rename). Add a test per form.

issues.suggested_fix: Outside script and scalar text, reject any line whose key's value starts with &, * or ! or with an alias, any line starting with '? ' or ': ' after the indent, and any key that is not a plain [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ followed by optional spaces and ':'. Allow \s* before ':' in RUN_KEY. Better still, parse with yaml.safe_load when PyYAML is available and walk jobs.*.steps.*.run and continue-on-error on the parsed tree.

issues.problem: The doc says the agent-plugins entries 'install ... with path: plugins/silver-bullet ... so published installs consume only that subtree'. But plugins/silver-bullet is mostly symlinks that leave the subtree (hooks -> ../../hooks, scripts -> ../../scripts, docs -> ../../docs, AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md, ...). It also has no .claude-plugin/ manifest, only .codex-plugin and .cursor-plugin. So either the install fetches the full tree (no shrink), or, under Codex --sparse, the links dangle. Unconfirmed: the agent-plugins repo and host loaders cannot be checked offline.
issues.evidence: ls -la plugins/silver-bullet in the worktree shows the symlinks to ../../hooks, ../../scripts and ../../docs, and no .claude-plugin directory.
issues.suggested_fix: Reword: the subtree path selects the manifest, while hooks and scripts come from the repository root through symlinks, so on-disk size is not reduced. Or verify a sparse Codex install resolves the links, and record that.
